title: Normalization of the regular coefficient unit
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and positive quotients $A_{n+1}=R/\varpi^{n+1}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$, use strict semilinear coefficient systems and their ordinary derived category and exact evaluations [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, def-coef-finite-adjunction-system-data]. For every scheme $W$, the actual degree-zero regular coefficient unit [def-sf-finite-adjunction-coefficient-unit] is normalized: for every $n\le m$ and every $P$ over $A_{n+1}$, precomposition with its quotient transition induces a bijection from maps out of its nth evaluation into $P$ to maps from its mth evaluation into the restricted $P$.

proof.text: Evaluation of the regular sequence-ring module is the regular finite module and its transition is the quotient homomorphism, on each section. Since this free rank-one module is flat, derived quotient extension is ordinary quotient extension. Multiplication identifies that extension with the target regular module. The derived scalar-extension/restriction adjunction then gives exactly the required bijection for every derived target P; the identity quotient gives the identity bijection.
